items.title: Rimac 宣布 Nevera 电动超跑即将停产，累计仅生产 71 辆
items.description: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，克罗地亚汽车制造商 Rimac 即将结束旗下 Nevera 纯电动超级跑车的生产。目前，公司正在制造最后 10 辆 Nevera R，预计这些车辆将在今年年底前全部交付客户。此后，该车将正式停产。 Rimac 创始人兼 CEO 马特 · 里马克（Mate Rimac）在一段 Instagram 视频中透露，自 2022 年开始交付以来， Rimac Automobili 总共生产了 71 辆 Nevera 系列超跑 。其中，标准版 Nevera 有 51 辆，性能更强的 Nevera R 有 20 辆。 2018 年，公司首次展示后来发展为 Nevera 的概念车型时， 原本计划生产 150 辆 。尽管最终产量远低于最初目标，马特 · 里马克对此仍然相当满意。 他在视频最后表示：“我认为，这仍然是一项相当了不起的成就。 它是全球销量最高的电动超级跑车 。如果没有它，就不会有今天的 Tourbillon，也不会有现在这座工厂。因此，它已经完成了自己的使命。我认为这是一辆非常酷的汽车…… 它将在汽车历史上占有一席之地。感谢所有车主，感谢你们参与这段不可思议

items.description: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，科技媒体 NeoWin 今天（11 月 12 日）发布博文，报道称本月补丁星期二面向 Windows 11 推送的累积更新中，微软收紧安全检查， 因此可能导致部分旧 PowerShell 脚本无法正常工作。 报道指出 Windows 11 系统在安装 11 月累积更新之后，对 PowerShell 脚本的签名及验证引入了更严格的文本编码检查，尤其是包含错误 UTF-8 编码的文件。Windows 11 此前版本在解码这些不规范的 PowerShell 脚本时，可能通过替换无效字符接受这些文件。 而新规则明确拒绝此类编码，因此旧脚本即使已经签名，也可能被识别为“未签名”，尝试重新签名时同样可能报错。 微软给出的处理办法是：将受影响脚本保存为有效的、带字节顺序标记（BOM）的 UTF-8 编码，检查内容后重新签名。对于需要批量处理的用户，微软还提供了修复工具，可扫描潜在编码问题，并尝试在保留现有签名的情况下修复文件，且不会覆盖原文件。 此次调整也不限于 Windows 11，微软相关指导还涵盖 Windows 10 企业版 LTSC 2021，以及包括 W

items.content: 就在刚刚，豆包工作正式宣布，平台接入 Kimi 3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 等多款第三方模型，并同步推出限时优惠活动。用户可以根据不同任务的需求，自主选择相应模型完成工作。 随着越来越多的大模型进入实际办公场景，用户在处理编程、文档写作、数据分析等任务时，对模型能力、响应速度和使用成本的要求也有所不同。 此次更新意味着，豆包工作进一步丰富了平台内的模型选择，让用户能够在同一个工作平台上使用不同厂商提供的 AI 模型，减少频繁切换工具的麻烦。 此前，豆包工作已经面向企业客户开放第三方模型。此次更新后，平台在模型选择页面进一步标注了各款模型的额度消耗倍率，方便用户直观了解不同模型的使用成本。 按照官方说明，模型的额度消耗倍率越低，通常意味着相应的模型调用成本越低。用户可以结合任务复杂程度、模型能力及额度消耗情况，选择适合自己的模型。 在价格方面，豆包工作还宣布推出全新的限时优惠计划。用户在工作日及节假日的指定优惠时段内，使用参与活动的模型，还可以享受额外的额度消耗优惠。

items.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
items.description: As soon as Wednesday evening, Nvidia's board could decide to remove its founder and CEO of 33 years.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports . Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company. On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman purported by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. On Wednesday evening, the New York Times reported that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him. Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world as it designs the chips that power the AI boom, but in the midst of Huang’s ongoing scandal , Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday. The stock is down about 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. According to Bloomberg, Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates that could potentially replace Huang as CEO. The sources said that Huang and Powell were captured on video “being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel” during a conference earlier this year. Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment. The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993. items.author: Anna Heim
items.content: Fractile , a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated . Alongside the likes of Axelera , Etched , and OLIX , this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production. However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips. As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source . Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot , its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual trade-off between memory and capacity. items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content: The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some in the industry see it as an issue that’s much larger than one man. The Chinese government has been active in economic espionage for decades, and with semiconductors at the center of the AI boom, there’s intense pressure to infiltrate any company involved. At the same time, many of the executives getting rich off that boom have made themselves easy targets. As CEO of investment intel firm Heron Intelligence, Nate Singer has a unique view into the problem. His firm works on corporate due diligence: Essentially, making sure companies know the relevant dirt before making a major acquisition or executive hire. And while the Nvidia case is particularly severe, Singer says there are lots of similar cases in the semiconductor industry that have stayed under the radar. “We’ve got former employees talking about behavior at senior executive levels,” Singer told TechCrunch, saying executives are “really crossing lines that should not be crossed.” In a widely circulated LinkedIn post , Singer detailed one case in which a CEO’s wife made an unexpected board room appearance, “screaming about her husband and another company exec flying around in the corporate jet with a couple young ladies (who also turned out to be state-sponsored actors).” It’s an alarming story, but an unfortunately common one. items.description: Sales of $10 billion represents an almost 50% jump from revenue of $6.7 billion the company recorded in the second quarter.
items.author: Ram Iyer
items.content: OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported , citing anonymous sources. If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year. OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said. OpenAI, one of the first to commercialize AI models, wasn’t exactly struggling to continue growing its top-line expansion — 18% growth on top of $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue is massive by any measure, especially compared to most software businesses. But it was seeing those gains be trumped by its archrival Anthropic, which has taken the lead in capturing the enterprise market for AI models and recently reported Q3 revenue of $17 billion . OpenAI’s broader focus helped it attract a large user base and gain popularity early on, and it says it has over a billion users , but it’s reasonable to assume most of those are free users or subscribers to its cheapest plans.
